record.original_question: For the KPZ equation on a uniformly growing domain with dilution, ∂ₜh = ν(t₀/t)^(2γ)∇²h + (λ/2)(t₀/t)^(2γ)(∇h)² − (dγ/t)h + γF t^(γ−1) + (t₀/t)^(dγ/2)ξ(x,t), the Hopf-Cole transformation leads to a nonlinear equation resembling a time-dependent, spatially distributed Gompertz differential equation. Can one find an explicit deterministic solution for this dilution KPZ dynamics, and what is its decorrelation threshold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the KPZ equation on a uniformly growing $d$-dimensional domain with dilution, written in comoving coordinates as
$$\partial_t h(x,t) = \nu\left(\tfrac{t_0}{t}\right)^{2\gamma}\nabla^2 h + \tfrac{\lambda}{2}\left(\tfrac{t_0}{t}\right)^{2\gamma}(\nabla h)^2 - \tfrac{d\gamma}{t}\,h + \gamma F\, t^{\gamma-1} + \left(\tfrac{t_0}{t}\right)^{d\gamma/2}\xi(x,t),$$
where $h(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}$ is the height field, $\nu>0$ is the surface tension, $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ the nonlinear coupling, $\gamma\ge 0$ the domain growth exponent, $t_0>0$ a reference time, $F\in\mathbb{R}$ a constant drive, and $\xi$ a Gaussian space-time white noise with $\langle\xi(x,t)\xi(x',t')\rangle=\delta^d(x-x')\delta(t-t')$.

Apply the Hopf–Cole transformation $u=\exp\!\left(\tfrac{\lambda}{2\nu}h\right)$ to obtain the multiplicative-noise equation
$$\partial_t u = \nu\left(\tfrac{t_0}{t}\right)^{2\gamma}\nabla^2 u - \tfrac{d\gamma}{t}\,u\ln(u) + \tfrac{\gamma F\lambda}{2\nu}\,t^{\gamma-1}\,u + \tfrac{\lambda}{2\nu}\left(\tfrac{t_0}{t}\right)^{d\gamma/2}\xi(x,t)\,u,$$
which is a time-dependent, spatially distributed analogue of the Gompertz ODE.

(a) Find an explicit closed-form solution of the deterministic version of this equation (i.e., with $\xi\equiv 0$), giving $u(x,t)$ and consequently $h(x,t)$ in terms of the initial data and the parameters $(\nu,\lambda,\gamma,F,t_0,d)$.

(b) Determine the decorrelation threshold of this deterministic dilution KPZ dynamics, i.e., the time scale (as a function of the parameters) beyond which spatial correlations of $h(x,t)$ inherited from the initial condition cease to be effectively transmitted by the dynamics.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for explicit solutions and decorrelation thresholds of the dilution KPZ equation on a uniformly growing domain (in its Hopf–Cole/Gompertz form) returned only general references on the standard KPZ equation, Hopf–Cole transform, and spatial decorrelation results — none addressing this specific dilution/growing-domain variant. No published resolution was identified, but absence of search hits is not conclusive evidence of openness.

status_evidence.title: Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of standard KPZ; no mention of dilution/growing-domain variant or Gompertz reduction.
status_evidence.claim: General KPZ literature does not record an explicit solution for the dilution KPZ on a growing domain.

status_evidence.title: Universality of slow decorrelation in KPZ growth
status_evidence.snippet: Treats slow decorrelation for standard KPZ-class growth, not the dilution growing-domain version.
status_evidence.claim: Decorrelation results in the literature target standard KPZ, not the proposed dilution variant.

status_evidence.title: Solving the KPZ equation - Hairer
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs solutions to the standard KPZ equation via regularity structures.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit deterministic solution to the time-dependent Gompertz-type form is provided.
